entries.definition: very irritable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Touchy about a particular subject rather than in general.
examples: he became prickly and spiteful

entries.definition: bright and pleasant; promoting a feeling of cheer
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Outward-facing: a cheery greeting is aimed at somebody.
examples: a cheery hello

entries.definition: very bad
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casual disgust - everyday, forceful, and slightly coarse.
examples: a lousy play

entries.definition: in an inhumane manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *inhumane*: the institutional word - it is conditions, treatment and policies that get called inhumane.
examples: the prisoners of war were treated inhumanely

entries.definition: marked by deliberate deceptiveness especially by pretending one set of feelings and acting under the influence of another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A near-archaic use, and the pun softens it - the double-dealing sounds almost like a skill.

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clinical and detached - the word on a chart, not at a graveside.

entries.definition: unrelenting and deadly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: *A mortal enemy* - deadly rather than pitiless, and archaic in flavour.
examples: mortal enemy

entries.definition: not wise in the ways of the world
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and faintly condescending - sophistication is assumed to be the goal.
examples: either too unsophisticated or too honest to promise more than he could deliver

entries.definition: very thin especially from disease or hunger or cold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Suggests thinness carved by hardship, illness or grief - sombre rather than insulting.
examples: a nightmare population of gaunt men and skeletal boys
Months of worry had left him gaunt.

entries.definition: sincerely earnest
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Religious first, and it carries the discipline of practice with it.
examples: devout wishes for their success

entries.definition: made dirty or foul
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainer form, common in reports about water and air.
examples: a building befouled with soot
breathing air fouled and darkened with factory soot

entries.definition: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and dated - the liver as the seat of a bad mood.

entries.definition: affecting extreme elegance in dress and manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same fault named after the person rather than the process.

entries.definition: in a stubborn unregenerate manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *stubborn*: mildly critical, and often affectionate - it can be said of a child or a stain.
examples: she remained stubbornly in the same position

entries.definition: offensively curious or inquisitive
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the act rather than the character - the person is doing it right now.
examples: prying eyes

entries.definition: concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Softer than *selfish* - it describes where attention sits rather than what was taken.
examples: What I can't believe is that people are so stupid and self-centered that they think they HAVE to comment on things they don't like.

entries.definition: laugh quietly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Quiet mocking laughter, aimed at someone rather than shared.

entries.definition: not counterfeit or copied
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Emphasis rather than proof - a veritable feast is not being authenticated.
examples: photographs taken in a veritable bull ring

entries.definition: lacking funds
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British slang, cheerfully blunt.
examples: ‘skint’ is a British slang term

entries.definition: limp and soiled as if dragged in the mud
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The older and rarer half of *bedraggled*, with the same sympathy.
examples: the beggar's bedraggled clothes
scarecrows in battered hats or draggled skirts

entries.definition: marked by extreme anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The anger has taken the person over; it describes a state, not an opinion.
examples: the enraged bull attached

entries.definition: having or showing no mercy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same judgement in the older negative form, and slightly more formal.

entries.definition: subdued or brought low in condition or status
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Not modesty at all: something was done to this person and it worked.
examples: a broken man
his broken spirit

entries.definition: having a difficult and contrary disposition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: American and fond as often as not; an ornery mule is being described, not blamed.

entries.definition: in a creaky manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *creaky*: also used of arguments and institutions, where it means old and barely holding.
examples: the old boat was moving along creakily

entries.definition: worn and broken down by hard use
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Describes the look of sorrow rather than the damage, which makes it oddly gentle.
examples: a woebegone old shack

entries.definition: being very thin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Measured against a medical standard rather than an opinion - the neutral clinical term.

entries.definition: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Kindness aimed at someone in difficulty; it presumes there is trouble to meet.
examples: sympathetic words

entries.definition: with patience; in a patient manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *patient*: endurance with an even temper - the temper is what distinguishes it from mere waiting.
examples: he patiently played with the child

entries.definition: incited, especially deliberately, to anger
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the blame on the other party outright: someone did this to them.
examples: the provoked animal attacked the child

entries.definition: having or showing self-esteem
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Self-possession that earns respect - pride carried well.
examples: a dignified reply to a rude question

entries.definition: criticize harshly or violently
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The metaphor is an animal attack - it says the criticism went past its target.
examples: The press savaged the new President

entries.definition: in a ravishing manner or to a ravishing degree
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *ravishing*: overwhelming beauty - lush and a little theatrical.
examples: she was ravishingly beautiful

entries.definition: vacuously or complacently and unconsciously foolish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *inane*: empty of sense - condemns the content, not the person.

entries.definition: having the capacity for thought and reason especially to a high degree
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The neutral, respectable word - approving without flourish.
examples: is there intelligent life in the universe?
an intelligent reading of a difficult text

entries.definition: contented to a fault with oneself or one's actions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The satisfaction is with oneself, and it is visible to everyone else.
examples: his self-satisfied dignity

entries.definition: marked by lack of attention or consideration or forethought or thoroughness; not careful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain accusation: attention was owed and not paid.
examples: careless about her clothes
forgotten by some careless person

entries.definition: concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same charge, aimed at a career rather than a single act.

entries.definition: (chiefly Scottish) agreeable and genial
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The commoner spelling of couthie, with the same Scots warmth.

entries.definition: ill-mannered and coarse and contemptible in behavior or appearance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The animal comparison again, here about manners rather than appetite.
examples: aristocratic contempt for the swinish multitude

entries.definition: concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Borrowed from developmental psychology, where it describes children without blaming them.
examples: I will never forgive her for her egocentric and shameful conduct towards Gilliatt

entries.definition: characterized by careless unconcern
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Warnings existed and were ignored; it presumes there was something to heed.
examples: the heedless generosity and the spasmodic extravagance of persons used to large fortunes

entries.definition: laugh nervously
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Nervous, suppressed laughter - faintly silly and easily condescended to.

entries.definition: express commendation of
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Borrows the gesture from the military; it praises formally and briefly, as an act of respect.
examples: I salute your courage!

entries.definition: having or proceeding from an innately kind disposition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hyphenated spelling of the same word, equally warm.

entries.definition: naive and easily deceived or tricked
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Inexperience with an expiry date: a state to be grown out of, not a fault.

entries.definition: in a shrewd manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *sapient*: latinate and cool - it is the species name doing double duty.
